description:
Anything for dogs around a town, county or point: everything dog-related nearby, grouped by kind: beaches, parks, trails, hotels, campgrounds, cabins, places to eat and rest areas, each sorted by distance, with the dog rule and citation for each. Answers "what can I do with my dog there?" for a named place.

Takes a town, county, area, region or neighborhood name (no coordinates needed) or a point. Small spelling slips are corrected and labeled. When nothing is inside the radius, the search widens on its own (to 30, 60, then 100 miles) and says so; when the data has nothing near at all, the answer lists the nearest records anyway, so there is always something to offer. A name the data does not know comes back with close matches (did_you_mean) and what to call next, not an error.

Examples:
  - "What can my dog do in Carmel?" -> place="Carmel"
  - "Dog beaches and parks around South Lake Tahoe" -> place="South Lake Tahoe", types=["beach","park"]
  - "Anything dog-friendly in Van Nuys?" -> place="Van Nuys"
  - "Anything dog-friendly within 5 miles of here" -> near={lat:36.6, lon:-121.9}, radius_miles=5

dogs_allowed_only.description: Leave out places where dogs are not allowed

near.description: A point instead of a town; give one of place or near

per_type.description: Nearest results to show per kind

place.description: A city, county, area, region or neighborhood in California or Nevada, e.g. "Monterey", "South Lake Tahoe", "Washoe County, NV", "Las Vegas", "East Bay", "Lake Tahoe", "Central Valley" or "Van Nuys". Small spelling slips are corrected and the answer says so.

radius_miles.description: Search radius in miles around the town or point (an area is its own boundary; the radius is ignored)

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

types.description: Kinds to include; all by default

name: dogpolicies_near

center.description: The point searched around; null when the place was not found

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

citation.description: Copy-ready citation: answer, source, date checked, record URL, license

confidence.description: stated: the place's own source says it; inferred_from_agency: an agency-wide rule; inherited_brand: the chain's policy, not confirmed by this hotel

freshness.description: fresh: inside its review interval; due: past it; stale: past twice it, confirm before you go; unreadable: the last check could not read the source

uid.description: Stable id that survives a rename

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

radius_widened_from.description: Set when the radius asked for held nothing and the search widened

title: What is near a town
